summary: Remove unused Git filesystem storage from Docker and OpenShift deployment templates to reflect database-backed application persistence.
userImpact: Core application data, including uploaded branding assets, models and version history, continues to persist in the database.

instructions: Updated templates no longer mount or provision the unused Git repository volume or backend PVC. Existing volumes and claims are not automatically deleted.
Existing GIT_REPOS_PATH values may be removed from local environment files; the current Git service does not read this setting.

configuration: Remove git_repos volume declarations and mounts from development, production, self-hosted and identity-rehearsal Compose configurations.
Remove the backend-git-repos PVC, its mount and the unused GIT_REPOS_PATH setting from OpenShift templates, environment examples, CI setup and verification runners.

notes: No database schema or application data changes are required.

documentation: Deployment and configuration references describe database-backed application persistence without a Git filesystem storage requirement.
knownLimitations: Optional plugins and deployment tooling can have independent storage requirements.
rollback: Restore the previous deployment templates and environment examples; no database rollback is needed.
validation: Compose rendering passed all five compose-render CI steps and the identity-rehearsal, pooled-tenancy and self-hosted configuration-bundle combinations.
OpenShift base and dev, staging and production overlays render without a backend application-data PVC; staging and production retain their configuration and secret projections.

CI contracts (218 tests), CI change detection (120 tests), focused deployment contracts (54 tests), shell syntax, configuration deployment, documentation boundary, package-version discipline and release-note preflight passed locally with Node.js 24.10.0 and pnpm 11.0.8.
No application source or database schema changed. Container startup, image smoke and external OpenShift rollout qualification were not run locally.
